title: Claude Ship
lede: Anthropic's post introducing Claude Ship lays out how Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals carry a pull request from review through fixes to a policy-based approval.

points: Code Review checks PRs from several angles, verifies findings adversarially, and offers Quick, Standard or Deep levels per repository.
PR Steward fixes failing checks, conflicts and review feedback but is built not to approve or merge; @claude stop makes it step back.
Claude Approvals reads a policy file on the default branch, working like a smarter CODEOWNERS, and can run in observe mode first.
A new /ship command in Claude Code pushes a change, opens the PR and works it toward merge.
Usage is billed on tokens, and it is unavailable to organizations on Zero Data Retention, HIPAA or customer-managed keys.

points.text: Several commenters already run similar pipelines by hand, often pairing models from different vendors so one reviews what the other wrote.
One commenter walks through each step of human review being handed to Claude and asks how merging got automated so fast.
Some say open-source tools can build the same flow with any model, and question betting on the product surviving.
Practical snags surface, such as the bundled /ship command overriding teams' own /ship skills with no way to disable just it.
